cards.body:
## Summary
Linga's screens are decided in four places that already disagree. Move the decision into one pure module, `lib/english/view.ts`: `lingaView(session, ui)` returns the TV's tag, title, caption, hero model, actions (each with an id and the command it runs), the line to speak and the answer target. LingaTV renders it, the phone's StartPanel and the PC test bar read its home state and answer target, and the LT driver prints it and derives its action list from it.

## Description
Today the TV's screen model is a 126-line if/else chain inside LingaTV.tsx (40-165), with nothing under test. The phone re-decides home with three of the TV's six states (LingaPhone.tsx:170-184). The PC test bar re-decides what takes a typed answer (LingaTestBar.tsx:15-26). The LT driver, the only eyes a text-live UAT run has (AG-4), hand-writes a third rendering of every screen and a hand list of 36 action ids (linga-text.cjs:208-306). Counted drift: (1) Resume on a paused scene sends 'pause' on the TV and 'resume' in LT; (2) the LT recap omits the phone's moment list, and the beginners run's theme 4 (4/4 Characters, a build item) quotes exactly that omitted string; (3) the test bar offers no answer during a quiz, while the phone and the driver do; (4) 'See my topics' from the verdict routes differently once a plan is done; (5) the phone home has no resume or plan-done state; (6) the driver exposes 2 of 8 menu entries. Every LT run, and every backlog drained from it, stands on the hand copy. So does every new Linga screen, which today has to be written four times.

## Flow
- view.ts: `lingaHome(s)` (six named states), `lingaView(s, ui)` -> `{screen, tag, title, caption, captionTag, hero:{kind,...data}, actions:[{id,label,help,run}], spoken, answer, recap}`, `viewText(view)` for the driver, and `VIEW_ACTION_IDS`.
- LingaTV keeps only JSX for each hero kind (ladder, topics, comparison, choices, message, track, menu), plus key handling and the audio hook fed by `view.spoken`.
- The LingaPhone StartPanel switches on `lingaHome`, and LingaTestBar uses `view.answer`.
- linga-text.cjs: `surface()` = `viewText(lingaView(...))` plus the phone reply affordance from `view.answer`. `run()` executes `action.run`, and ACTIONS = VIEW_ACTION_IDS.
- Gate: `cd desk && npm test`, `node --check uat/driver/linga-text.cjs`, and a Playwright capture of the Linga TV screens against a second dev server (config.md TV row).

## Expected impact
An LT run judges what the TV and phone actually offer. Findings that come from the driver's copy stop reaching the backlog: the recap theme would have been judged against the moment list the phone already shows. The TV screen logic gets its first tests. A new Linga screen or action is written once. The ladder-help card (slot B) and any later Linga screen land in one place rather than four.

## Evaluation
Claim: one screen model removes the six counted drifts and makes the TV's screen logic testable
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (cases 7-8 are GUARDs, green by construction once view.ts exists); 4 implementations of screen knowledge, 6 counted drifts
After: 8 of 8; 1 implementation, 0 drifts in the parity sweep
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: architecture

cards.title: Help that answers the question on screen: a code-run rescue ladder per turn
shared_surfaces: uat/driver/linga-text.cjs (uat context; also in slot A's write set - build A first or rebase B onto it)
acceptance: case 1 (linga-rules-test, stub engine): the turn stub returns reply 'Which date do you need?' with help {simpler:'What day do you come?', meaning:'date: the day, like Friday', starter:'I need the room on …'}; three 'cue' commands -> c.cue walks simpler, then meaning, then starter; c.help.rung is 1, 2, 3; c.supported is false, false, true

case 2 (linga-rules-test): the Tomas case. Turn 1's partner line asks the dog's name (ladder A) and one cue reveals A.simpler. Turn 2's partner line asks about the ball (ladder B). A cue now -> c.cue is B.simpler and never any ladder-A text or the scene's static cue

case 3 (linga-rules-test): a reply sent after rung 2 at most -> the turn's learner record and its observations carry supported:false (help that supplied no wording can still earn independent evidence). A reply after rung 3 -> supported:true

case 4 (linga-rules-test): withholding. Right after the turn commits, JSON.stringify(getSession()) contains none of the three ladder strings. After one cue it contains only the simpler line (unrevealed rungs stay in server memory, like check.ts's answer keys)

case 5 (linga-rules-test): a malformed ladder (starter 'I need a room for Friday.' is a complete sentence; simpler equals the partner line) -> the bad rungs are dropped by help.ts. The turn still commits its partner reply and evidence. With every rung invalid, cue falls back to scene.cue with supported:true (today's behaviour)
case 6 (linga-rules-test): the 'cue' command makes zero engine calls (the stub's call counter is unchanged). A ladder lost to a server restart (help map cleared) falls back to scene.cue
case 7 GUARD: (linga-rules-test) the stub replies with no help field, as every existing test does -> cue gives scene.cue with supported:true; the quiz, moment and coach tests stay green unchanged

cards.body:
## Summary
When a learner is stuck, 'Give me a cue' hands back the same scene-level line on every turn. Linga should answer the question actually on the screen, one step at a time. Each partner line comes with its own three-rung rescue ladder: said more simply, what it means, a way to start. Code reveals one rung per request, decides which rung makes the reply supported, and keeps the unrevealed rungs off the session.

## Description
The cue is `scene.cue` (conversation.ts:134-135), a single 'Try: ...' per scene or plan topic. The LT beginners run found stale help for 3 of 3 stuck Characters, and ranked it first: Tomas was asked for the dog's name three times after naming Pip, Petra was asked for the booking number again, and Viktor got weather help for colours. Because the only help also marks the reply supported (:135), a learner who needs any help can never earn independent evidence (rules.ts:30), which is theme 3 of the same run. The design already specifies the ladder (LINGA-CONVERSATION-DESIGN.md:53). Opening, turn and replay each already produce the partner's line in one model call. The same call returns that line's ladder: simpler (a shorter question in common words, no answer supplied), meaning (the unknown word explained, for a beginner possibly in their own language), and starter (an incomplete opening ending in an ellipsis). help.ts validates it: the simpler line must be shorter than the partner line and different from it, the starter must be short and unfinished, and a rung that fails is dropped. The ladder is kept in server memory keyed by partner turn. The rules decide in code, the model only phrases: rungs are revealed in order, and only the starter makes the reply supported. The TV caption tag names the rung ('Said more simply', 'What it means', 'A way to start'). The phone button reads 'Help me answer', then 'More help'. After the last rung, 'Choose a phrase' stays the recognition fallback.

## Flow
- The partner speaks, and its ladder is validated and stored server-side under the turn id.
- Learner taps 'Help me answer': code reveals rung 1 in the caption, and the reply stays unsupported.
- Taps again: rung 2. Again: rung 3, and from then on the reply is supported.
- The next partner line brings a new ladder, so help cannot go stale.
- With no ladder (old stub, restart, invalid rungs), the cue falls back to today's scene.cue.

## Expected impact
Help stops going stale on the path every stuck beginner takes, which was the top-ranked finding of the latest LT run. Learners who only needed the question said more simply keep independent credit, so 'On your own' becomes reachable for the learners who ask for help, and supported is no longer the only way through. A cue costs no extra model call or wait, where a separate help call on the CLI engine would take 17-52 s (LINGA-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md:52). The starter rung withholds more than today's full 'Try:' sentences.

## Evaluation
Claim: help answers the current partner turn, walks a code-ordered ladder, and leaves early-rung replies unsupported
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (case 7 is a GUARD, green before by design); cue text is identical across turns in 3 of 3 J4 transcripts
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance cases written as failing tests first
Result: better
Gate: contract (Conversation gains optional `help:{forTurn,rung}` and cue text now varies per turn; consumers: desk/src/english/LingaTV.tsx, desk/src/english/LingaPhone.tsx, desk/src/english/LingaTestBar.tsx (reads conversation, unaffected), uat/driver/linga-text.cjs, desk/src/lib/session/store.ts load at :191, POST /api/english response body)

critic.deck_line: Approve: help follows the partner's current question, costs no extra model call, and stops marking every helped reply as supported.
